target.title: feat(memory-wiki): add wiki_open_items tool to list unresolved questions and contradictions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`memory-wiki` already detects unresolved knowledge-health items — open questions, page/claim contradictions, and low-confidence pages/claims — but they are only reachable as side effects: rendered into the compiled `reports/*.md` dashboards or surfaced inline by `wiki_lint`'s structural pass. There is no first-class, machine-readable way for an agent (or a future maintenance flow) to *enumerate* just the open items, with their text and page location, so they can be worked through one at a time.

## Why does it matter / user impact?

Agents that want to help a user resolve accumulated wiki debt (answer open questions, reconcile contradictions, re-confirm low-confidence claims) currently have to scrape a human-oriented dashboard or re-run a broad lint and parse its prose. This adds a small, read-only `wiki_open_items` tool that returns a structured list of exactly those items, filterable by kind and limit. It is the enabling primitive for interactive "work through the open items" resolution flows (see #105494) without committing the project to any particular UX for that yet.

## Why in core (extensions/) rather than a third-party plugin?

Per CONTRIBUTING, most features should be third-party plugins. This one is deliberately *not*: it is a thin read-only accessor over `memory-wiki`'s own already-internal derivations (`readQueryableWikiPages`, the contradiction-cluster builders, and `collectWikiClaimHealth`). A third-party plugin could not reach those without either the `unsafe-local` private-path escape hatch or duplicating the parsing/derivation logic — both of which would be strictly worse than exposing one more tool from the plugin that already owns this data. It registers no new config, no new dependencies, and no new surface beyond a single tool that mirrors the existing `wiki_lint` shape.

## Evidence

Change set (7 files, +321/-9):
- `src/open-items.ts` (new) — pure `deriveMemoryWikiOpenItems(pages)` + disk `collectMemoryWikiOpenItems(rootDir)`; enumerates 5 kinds (open-question, page-contradiction, claim-contradiction, low-confidence-page, low-confidence-claim).
- `src/open-items.test.ts` (new) — 3 cases (all kinds; cross-page claim-contradiction cluster; clean vault → empty).
- `src/tool.ts` — `createWikiOpenItemsTool` with `kinds`/`limit` filters, mirroring `wiki_lint`.
- `index.ts` — registers `wiki_open_items`.
- `index.test.ts` — tool-registry assertions updated.
- `openclaw.plugin.json` — declares `wiki_open_items` in `contracts.tools`.
- `docs/plugins/memory-wiki.md` — documents the new agent tool.

Validation (all run in a clean Cloudflare crabbox container against `upstream/main`):
- `pnpm build` ✓
- `tsgo:extensions` + `tsgo:extensions:test` ✓
- `oxlint` 0 errors / 0 warnings ✓
- `oxfmt --check` ✓
- `test:extension memory-wiki` → **307/307** ✓
- `test:contracts:plugins` → **986/986** (43 files, incl. the plugin-registration contract lane that enforces the manifest tool contract) ✓
- `format:docs:check` + markdownlint → clean ✓

### Real behavior proof

`collectMemoryWikiOpenItems` run against a seeded vault returns the expected structured items:

```
$ node -e '... collectMemoryWikiOpenItems(vault) ...'
[
  { kind: "open-question", page: "topics/routing.md", text: "Is the gateway bound to 0.0.0.0 intentionally?" },
  { kind: "page-contradiction", page: "topics/routing.md", text: "conflicts with topics/network.md on bind address" },
  { kind: "claim-contradiction", page: "topics/network.md", text: "\"LAN is open\" vs \"LAN is firewalled\"" },
  { kind: "low-confidence-claim", page: "topics/network.md", text: "gateway bind is temporary (confidence 0.3)" }
]
```

Filtering (`kinds: ["open-question"]`, `limit: 1`) narrows the result as expected; a clean vault returns `[]`.

## AI assistance disclosure

This PR was authored with assistance from Claude Code (Claude Opus 4.8). A local `codex review --base origin/main` was run; it flagged one P1 (the tool was registered in `index.ts` but missing from `openclaw.plugin.json` `contracts.tools`, which the plugin registry and contract test enforce), which is fixed in this branch. The re-review returned clean.

Related: #105494

---

## Appendix — changes after review (`d6ba841b`)

Addressing the ClawSweeper/Codex review. Full point-by-point response and a real invocation proof are in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/105550#issuecomment-4952351092).

- **Real competing-claim text [P1].** For `claim-contradiction` items, `cluster.label` is only the shared claim id (`claim-health.ts:216`), so the item text was an opaque id. The derivation now builds the `text` from the actual conflicting statements and carries each one as structured data on a new `variants: [{ text, status, pagePath, pageTitle, confidence? }]` field; the rendered output shows the conflict directly.
- **Provider-safe schema [P1].** The `kinds` filter now uses the plugin SDK `stringEnum(WIKI_OPEN_ITEM_KINDS)` helper (flat `{ type: "string", enum: [...] }`) instead of a literal union that serialized to `anyOf`, which some provider tool-schema validators reject.
- **Filtered counts [P2].** `details.counts` is recomputed from the returned (filtered/limited) items via a shared `countMemoryWikiOpenItems()` helper; the whole-vault tally is exposed separately as `details.vaultCounts`.
- **Tool-level tests.** Added `createWikiOpenItemsTool` tests covering the flat-enum schema shape, competing-claim output, `kinds` filtering, `limit`, and the `counts` vs `vaultCounts` semantics (the prior tests only exercised the pure derivation).

Re-validated: `test:extension memory-wiki` 310 passed, `test:contracts:plugins` 986 passed, `tsgo:extensions`(+`:test`) clean, `lint:extensions` 0/0, `oxfmt --check` clean, `build` clean.
